name: Downtown and Dongdamen Night Market
tagline: The city centre, with the biggest night market on the east coast
description: Hualien's compact downtown around Zhongshan Road, with the Dongdamen night market at its eastern edge running down towards the sea. It holds the shops, the banks, the guesthouses and the restaurants, and the whole of it can be crossed on foot or by bicycle in minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the night market, the shops and the station within a short ride
pros: Dongdamen night market at the edge of the district
All services, banks and shops close by
cons: The highest rents in the town, though still modest
Busy with visitors in the Taroko season

name: Hualien Station Area
tagline: Around the railway, where the Taipei train and the rentals are
description: The district around Hualien station, the arrival point for everyone taking the coastal railway from Taipei, with hotels, scooter rental shops, the tour operators for Taroko and a growing cluster of newer apartments. Practical rather than pleasant, and the best-connected part of town.
bestFor: Stays built around the train to Taipei and scooter rental for the gorge
pros: Trains to Taipei in two hours from the doorstep
Scooter rental and Taroko operators concentrated here
cons: Fifteen minutes from the night market

name: Qixingtan and the Northern Coast
tagline: The pebble beach north, facing the open Pacific
description: The crescent of grey pebble beach a few kilometres north of the city, backed by the coastal highway with the mountains rising behind and nothing between you and the Pacific. Guesthouses and small hotels line the road, and the water here is deep and not for casual swimming.
bestFor: Stays that want the Pacific and the mountains framing every view
pros: The open Pacific and the mountains in one view
Quiet and much less built up than the city
Whale watching departs from the harbour nearby
cons: The water is deep and unsafe for swimming

name: Taroko Gorge Approach (20 km north)
tagline: Up the Liwu river, at the mouth of the marble canyon
description: The settlements at the entrance to Taroko National Park, where the Liwu river comes out of a marble canyon thousands of feet deep. Guesthouses and homestays sit along the approach road, some run by Truku indigenous families. Access to parts of the park has been restricted since the 2024 earthquake.
bestFor: Stays built entirely around the gorge, with the town accepted as a drive
pros: Taroko's trails and the canyon at the door
cons: Earthquake damage has closed parts of the park
Thirty minutes into Hualien and a vehicle is essential

name: Ji'an and the Rift Valley Edge
tagline: South of the city, rice fields between the mountain ranges
description: The township immediately south where Hualien gives way to the East Rift Valley, a corridor of rice paddies running between the coastal range and the Central Mountains. Housing is village and low-rise, rents are the lowest in the area, and the cycling through the fields is exceptional.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space, rice fields and the lowest rents
pros: The lowest rents in the area
Rice-field cycling between two mountain ranges
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes into the city
A scooter or car is necessary
